## From a plate photograph to a matched response

This guide introduces the FunMel workflow: analyze plate photographs, inspect
segmentation masks, organize experimental metadata, calculate matched-control
melanization coefficients, assess treatment effects and export comparison
figures. FunMel retains the original MycoHalo functions for compatibility.

The first worked example uses a bundled measured dataset from a 14-day
confrontation assay. Subsequent examples use simulated plates and measurements
to demonstrate image analysis and statistical methods. All runnable examples
in this guide use bundled or simulated inputs; no photograph download is needed.

The default assay has four approximately round *Zymoseptoria tritici* colonies
surrounding a central fungal colony and its halo candidate. Target-colony MI
quantifies darkness in the four *Z. tritici* colonies. The central fungus and
halo are measured separately and excluded from those MI summaries.
A known inoculation layout supplies search
regions and seeds. Detected outlines need not be round. These are image classes,
not automated species identification. A central colour zone is a halo candidate,
not a confirmed inhibition boundary.


> **The assay at a glance**  
> Four target *Zymoseptoria tritici* colonies surround a central fungal colony.
> FunMel measures target-colony darkness and geometry, separates the central
> partner and halo candidate, and compares each treatment with its own controls.

### Follow the workflow

| Step | Action | Result |
|:---|:---|:---|
| **1 · Analyze** | Set the plate layout and dish diameter | Target-colony measurements |
| **2 · Review** | Inspect masks, calibration and warnings | Documented quality decisions |
| **3 · Match** | Identify independent plates and their control sets | Verified experimental metadata |
| **4 · Compare** | Calculate matched coefficients and assess a supported model | Descriptive responses and, when justified, inference |
| **5 · Communicate** | Export plate-level figures and tables | Traceable results for reporting |

**Three essentials before starting:** MI is an image-darkness proxy, not melanin
concentration. Colonies within a dish are subsamples, not independent plates.
Each treatment uses only the controls assigned to its matching set.

## Install FunMel

Install a GitHub-hosted copy of the package using `remotes`. R >= 4.1 and
source-compilation tools are required: Xcode Command Line Tools on macOS,
the matching Rtools release on Windows, or an R development toolchain and
ImageMagick development libraries on Linux.

```{r github-install, eval=FALSE}
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("mghotbi/FunMel")
library(FunMel)
```

The source repository is [mghotbi/FunMel](https://github.com/mghotbi/FunMel).
The default installation uses its default branch. To select a release tag
or another branch, add `ref="TAG_OR_BRANCH"`.

To include the locally installed vignette:

```{r github-install-vignette, eval=FALSE}
install.packages(c("remotes", "knitr", "rmarkdown"))
remotes::install_github("mghotbi/FunMel",
                        build_vignettes=TRUE, dependencies=TRUE)
vignette("FunMel", package="FunMel")
```

Vignette building requires Pandoc, normally supplied with RStudio. Private
repositories require GitHub authentication. Restart R before replacing a loaded
FunMel installation. For a downloaded source archive, use
`install.packages(file.choose(), repos=NULL, type="source")` instead.

This guide introduces the FunMel workflow: analyze plate photographs, inspect
segmentation masks, organize experimental metadata, calculate matched-control
melanization coefficients, assess treatment effects and export comparison

to demonstrate image analysis and statistical methods. All runnable examples

The default assay has four approximately round *Zymoseptoria tritici* colonies

## Worked example: one control and three treatment plates per set
>>>>>>> origin/Rhizosphere-nitrogen-fate

The bundled 14-day dataset contains twenty photographs organized into five
matching sets. Each set contains one control dish and three treatment dishes,
with four target *Z. tritici* colonies per dish. Metadata has twenty plate rows;
the measurement table has eighty colony rows. This design is used to demonstrate
shared-control matching. Other experiments may have different replicate counts
and control arrangements, which must be recorded explicitly in their metadata.

```{r own-metadata}
real_meta <- read.csv(system.file("extdata","14_day_example","metadata.csv",
                                 package="FunMel"),stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
real_colonies <- read.csv(system.file("extdata","14_day_example","colonies.csv",
                                     package="FunMel"),stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
validate_metadata(real_meta)
knitr::kable(real_meta[real_meta$set_id=="A33_1_14_days",
                       c("file","plate_id","set_id","treatment","replicate")])
```

The same four-row structure applies to A60, B20, B22 and B37, with each set's own
control. The control replicate is 1 and the three treatment replicates are 1–3.
Replicate numbers do not define one-to-one pairing here: all three treatment
plates use their set's single control. Folder-derived treatment identities and
experimental mappings are provisional. Each control dish appears once in the
metadata and serves as the denominator for all treatment plates in its set.

## 1. Analyze and review a plate
=======
## 1. Analyze a plate and inspect its masks
>>>>>>> origin/Rhizosphere-nitrogen-fate

```{r first-image, fig.height=5.5}
lay <- plate_layout(centre="none")
sim <- simulate_plate(width=400,height=500,layout=lay,seed=21)
control <- analyze_plate(sim$image,layout=lay,id="synthetic_control",
                         n_boot=20,verbose=FALSE)
control$colonies[,c("colony_id","detected","MI_mean","area_mm2")]
plot_qc(control)
```

There is one measurement row per target colony. The overlay shows boundaries and
labels; the resolved-object panel shows the assigned regions. Four detected
regions are not proof of four correct biological objects. Check dish scale,
colony boundaries, reflections, central-object assignment and warnings.

```{r fungal-image, fig.height=5.5}
fungal_layout <- plate_layout(centre="fungus",rotation_deg=10)
fungal_sim <- simulate_plate(width=400,height=500,layout=fungal_layout,seed=22)
confrontation <- analyze_plate(fungal_sim$image,layout=fungal_layout,
                               id="synthetic_fungal",n_boot=20,verbose=FALSE)
confrontation$plate_summary[,c("central_partner_type","central_detected","halo_status")]
plot_qc(confrontation)
```

For fungal confrontation photographs, use `centre="fungus"`; control plates
use `centre="none"`. Pass an image path rather than `sim$image` and enter the
actual dish diameter:

```{r real-single, eval=FALSE}
img <- file.choose()
r <- analyze_plate(img,layout=plate_layout(centre="fungus"),
                   dish_diameter_mm=90,keep_images=TRUE)
plot_qc(r)
r$warnings
```

`keep_images=TRUE` allows later QC plotting. Batch results save QC PNGs but drop
large image arrays. Mean MI is `100 - L*` on retained, non-specular colony-interior
pixels: higher MI means darker images, not measured pigment concentration.

## 2. Set the inoculation layout
=======
## 2. Adapt the layout to new photographs
>>>>>>> origin/Rhizosphere-nitrogen-fate

```{r layouts}
plate_layout(centre="fungus",rotation_deg=15,radius_frac=0.5)
positions <- data.frame(id=c("N","E","S","W"),
                        x_rel=c(0,0.5,0,-0.5),y_rel=c(-0.5,0,0.5,0))
plate_layout(centre="fungus",positions=positions)
```

Coordinates are relative to the dish radius: x increases rightward and y
downward. `radius_mm` can set physical inoculation spacing. `search_frac` controls
core-search radius. Do not enlarge it indiscriminately to capture unrelated
growth. Optional numeric `rotation_deg`, `radius_frac`, `radius_mm`, `search_frac`,
`start_deg` and `n_colonies` metadata columns are read by `layout_by_treatment()`.
Explicit layout arguments take priority. Arbitrary image names and supported
layouts are allowed; severely merged colonies, reflections or uncertain class
identity still need review/training or manual analysis.

## 3. Match treatments to their controls
=======
## 3. Metadata defines which control is relevant
>>>>>>> origin/Rhizosphere-nitrogen-fate

One row is one independently prepared dish photographed once. Four colonies on
one plate are subsamples. Multiple photographs of the same dish are repeated
observations, not independent biological replicates.

| Field | Required interpretation |
|---|---|
| `file`, `relative_file` | Unique basename and optional path from the photo root |
| `plate_id` | Unique biological plate ID |
| `set_id` | Matching control set, often a batch |
| `treatment` | `control` or a consistent intervention name |
| `centre_model` | `none` for controls; `fungus` for fungal confrontation |
| `partner_type` | Biological partner type |
| `zymo_strain`, `day`, `medium` | Recommended context, complete and constant within a set if supplied |
| `metadata_confirmed` | TRUE after experimental mapping is verified |
| `qc_pass` | TRUE after acceptable mask and calibration review; required for finalization |

A treatment in S1 uses only S1 controls. Separate treatment-control experiments
need separate set IDs. Several treatments can legitimately share controls within
one batch: put all those plates in one set and list each control once. Do not
copy a shared control under new plate IDs. The same treatment label across sets
must mean the same intervention. Set IDs need not be folder names.

```{r metadata}
demo <- example_experiment(seed=42)
# Assign fungal labels to the two simulated treatment groups.
fungal_labels <- stats::setNames(c("fungus_A", "fungus_B"),
  setdiff(unique(as.character(demo$metadata$treatment)), "control"))
for (component in c("metadata", "colonies")) {
  d <- demo[[component]]
  d$treatment <- ifelse(d$treatment == "control", "control",
    fungal_labels[as.character(d$treatment)])
  for (field in intersect(c("centre_model", "partner_type"), names(d)))
    d[[field]] <- ifelse(d$treatment == "control", "none", "fungus")
  demo[[component]] <- d
}
validate_metadata(demo$metadata)
with(demo$metadata,table(set_id,treatment))
knitr::kable(head(demo$metadata[,c("file","plate_id","set_id","treatment","centre_model")]))
```

This synthetic design has three shared-control batches, each with control,
`fungus_A` and `fungus_B` and three independent plates per group. Its true MI
increments are 8 and 15, with added plate and colony variation. Plate IDs are
unambiguous; treatment C must not reuse an ID like C1 that also names a control.

```{r metadata-template, eval=FALSE}
make_metadata("photos",recursive=TRUE)
# Edit photos/plate_metadata.csv: fill experimental fields, do not guess them.
meta <- read.csv("photos/plate_metadata.csv",stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
files <- file.path("photos",meta$relative_file)
validate_metadata(meta,files)
# Alternative for any original photo ZIP, including enclosing folders:
files <- prepare_photo_archive("original_photos.zip",meta,"extracted_photos")
```

The template records provenance but leaves unknown experimental fields blank and
`metadata_confirmed=FALSE`. Validation checks unique files/plates, complete set
IDs, controls within each set and constant recorded matching contexts. Different
strains, days or media should have separate set IDs. Final pooling of multiple
recorded contexts requires an explicit `pool_contexts=TRUE` decision. It is not
a default biological recommendation.

The twenty-row case-study metadata is available as
`inst/examples/metadata_14_day_case_study.csv`, introduced at the start of this
guide. Use it as a worked example; create a separate metadata table for each
new experiment rather than reusing its assignments.

## 4. Calculate the melanization coefficient
=======
## 4. Calculate replicate responses, then descriptive treatment summaries
>>>>>>> origin/Rhizosphere-nitrogen-fate

Average target-colony MI within each plate, giving each colony equal weight.
Then average independent plate means within set and treatment, giving each plate
equal weight. The ratio is

\[
MI_p=\frac{1}{n_p}\sum_j MI_{pj},\qquad
MC_{s,t}=\frac{\operatorname{mean}_{p\in(s,t)} MI_p}
{\operatorname{mean}_{p\in(s,control)} MI_p}.
\]

```{r exact-coefficient}
d <- data.frame(plate_id=rep(c("C01","T01","T02","T03"),each=4),
                set_id="S1",treatment=rep(c("control","A","A","A"),each=4),
                colony_id=rep(c("TL","TR","BR","BL"),4),
                MI_mean=rep(c(40,48,52,56),each=4))
mc <- melanization_coefficient(d)
mc$plate_means
mc$per_plate_coefficients[,c("plate_id","melanization_coefficient")]
mc$coefficients[,c("MI_treatment_mean","MI_control_mean","melanization_coefficient")]
```

The replicate ratios are 1.2, 1.3 and 1.4; the treatment coefficient is
`mean(48,52,56)/40 = 1.3`. Independent plate measurements remain available for
analysis. This is not a mean of position-specific ratios. The partner is excluded
using target flags/central IDs. Missing target MI is an error by default;
`na_action="omit"` is an explicit documented-exclusion option. A whole unusable
plate remains unavailable. A nonpositive control denominator gives no ratio.

If a treatment occurs in several sets, its overall descriptive coefficient is
an equal-set mean of matched ratios, not a ratio against pooled unrelated controls.

```{r pooling}
x <- data.frame(plate_id=c("C1","T1","C2","T2"),set_id=c("S1","S1","S2","S2"),
                treatment=c("control","A","control","A"),colony_id="TL",
                MI_mean=c(20,40,80,80))
z <- melanization_coefficient(x)$coefficients
z[,c("set_id","melanization_coefficient")]
mean(z$melanization_coefficient) # 1.5; pooled 120/100 would be 1.2
```

A ratio of 1.3 is not evidence of 30% more melanin. MI is an image-darkness proxy.
Replicate-ratio SD/SE does not include uncertainty in a shared control denominator.

## 5. Assess treatment effects
=======
## 5. Assess treatments while retaining independent plates
>>>>>>> origin/Rhizosphere-nitrogen-fate

```{r assessment}
a <- assess_experiment(demo$colonies,comparison_scope="common_sets")
a$status
knitr::kable(a$overall_coefficients,digits=3)
# Preserve small p-values in the displayed tables; do not round them to zero.
format_tests <- function(x) {
  for(nm in intersect(c("p_value","p_adjusted"),names(x)))
    x[[nm]] <- base::format.pval(x[[nm]],digits=2,eps=0.001)
  x
}
knitr::kable(format_tests(a$overall_effects),digits=3)
knitr::kable(format_tests(a$treatment_comparisons),digits=3)
```

The descriptive ratios and inferential effects are different outputs. The mixed
model uses original colony MI with one random intercept per independent plate:

\[
MI_{spj}=\mu_{s,t(p)}+b_p+\epsilon_{spj},\quad
b_p\sim N(0,\sigma^2_{plate}),\quad \epsilon_{spj}\sim N(0,\sigma^2).
\]

Every observed set-treatment cell has its own fixed mean. `lme4` fits this model;
`lmerTest` gives Satterthwaite contrast inference. Within-set effects subtract
that set's control. A-versus-B compares matched effects, preserving shared-control
covariance. No test treats treatment averages as biological replicates. An
explicit `method="plate_means"` fits the same cell-specific fixed means to one
arithmetic mean per plate; with unequal colony counts it need not match the mixed
model's weighting exactly.

`comparison_scope="common_sets"` uses shared sets only; an absent common set gives
`no_common_sets`. The default `matched_effects` uses each treatment's observed
sets and flags different coverage. A treatment observed only in one batch cannot
automatically be separated from batch-specific effects. Holm-adjusted p values
are reported separately from unadjusted contrast-wise confidence intervals.

### How this relates to the usual treatment-plus-batch model

The confrontation-assay principle is retained: independent replicate measurements,
own-batch control normalization for interpretation, and modelling that accounts
for experimental structure. FunMel's cell-specific model estimates effects in
observed sets; it does **not** fit a common treatment effect across random batches.
An additive model instead assumes treatment differences are common across batches.
For a sufficiently crossed design, the following is an advanced alternative on
individual plate means, not treatment averages:

```{r additive-model}
pm <- melanization_coefficient(demo$colonies)$plate_means
additive <- lm(MI_plate ~ treatment + factor(set_id),data=pm)
coef(additive)
```

This example is separate from `assess_experiment()`, not an automatic fallback.
Check estimability, residual variance and whether a common treatment effect is
scientifically justified. A random-batch model such as
`lme4::lmer(MI_plate ~ treatment + (1 | set_id), data=pm)` additionally requires
an appropriate population-of-batches interpretation and enough batches to estimate
variance. Very few batches can make this unstable. More complex factorial,
longitudinal, spatial or heteroscedastic designs need their own models.

### Replication and diagnostics

The built-in assessment requires at least two independent plates per cell and
within-plate replication for its mixed model. This is a conservative computational
guard, not a universal requirement of all confrontation assays or proof of power.
One control plate still permits a descriptive ratio. Some sparse designs may
support other justified models; additional assumptions must not be hidden.

```{r sparse-design}
sparse <- suppressWarnings(assess_experiment(d))
sparse$status # insufficient_plate_replication
```

Singular fits, convergence problems and insufficient replication return explicit
status and withhold inferential tables. No significance test is silently substituted.

```{r diagnostics, fig.width=7.2, fig.height=3.5}
a$diagnostics$plates_per_cell
a$diagnostics$variance_components
op <- par(mfrow=c(1,2))
plot(fitted(a$model),residuals(a$model),xlab="Fitted MI",ylab="Residual")
abline(h=0,lty=2)
qqnorm(residuals(a$model));qqline(residuals(a$model))
par(op)
```

Spatial block-bootstrap intervals describe within-image pixel sampling, not
plate-to-plate biological variation. Normality and equal residual variance remain
model assumptions. Account for review/exclusion decisions and design limitations.

## 6. Process and finalize an experiment
=======
## 6. Process a real batch, review it and reuse saved measurements
>>>>>>> origin/Rhizosphere-nitrogen-fate

```{r real-batch, eval=FALSE}
out <- analyze_plates(files,metadata=meta,
                      layout=function(row) layout_by_treatment(row),
                      qc_dir="FunMel_results/qc")
saveRDS(out,"FunMel_results/image_analysis.rds")
out$failed
out$coefficient_error
# STOP and inspect every QC image, measurement warning and metadata mapping.
# Correct images/masks if needed. Then edit the CSV's confirmation/review flags.
reviewed_meta <- read.csv("photos/plate_metadata.csv",stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
reviewed <- finalize_analysis(out,reviewed_meta)
write.csv(reviewed$melanization_coefficient,
          "FunMel_results/matched_coefficients.csv",row.names=FALSE)
saveRDS(reviewed,"FunMel_results/reviewed_analysis.rds")
```

`finalize_analysis()` requires explicit complete logical `metadata_confirmed=TRUE`
and `qc_pass=TRUE`. These record user decisions, not automatic biological proof.
It applies verified labels to saved measurements without repeating image processing.
A changed central-partner recipe or layout requires reanalysis. Failed images must
be resolved before finalization. Do not silently discard an inconvenient replicate.
The generic `scripts/analyse_experiment.R` saves measurement tables, statuses and
session information and separates the review stage from final assessment.

## 7. Export figures and statistics
=======
## 7. Export a treatment comparison figure
>>>>>>> origin/Rhizosphere-nitrogen-fate

```{r comparison, fig.height=5.2}
plot_treatment_comparison(demo,
  labels=c(fungus_A="Fungal partner A",fungus_B="Fungal partner B"))
```

```{r figure-export, eval=FALSE}
p <- plot_treatment_comparison(reviewed,file="FunMel_results/treatment_comparison")
# Vector PDF/SVG, 600-dpi PNG and _statistics.csv are written.
attr(p,"FunMel_statistics") # means, SDs, independent plate counts, descriptive delta_MI
```

Panel A displays independent plate MI means and matching controls. Panel B
displays treatment replicate ratios and the set's ratio of means. Outlined squares are controls; coloured circles are treatment plates. Lower
diamonds show treatment means, with bars spanning mean ± one between-plate SD.
Each row reports control and treatment mean MI, treatment SD, coefficient and
coefficient SD. A single control plate has no estimable SD (shown as unavailable). Shared controls remain shared,
not new replicates. Coefficient SD measures treatment variability conditional on
the shared control mean; it excludes denominator uncertainty. These SDs are not
confidence intervals. The separate model results from `assess_experiment()` are
needed for supported inferential comparisons. Inferential estimates and confidence intervals are reported separately by
`assess_experiment()` when the design and model diagnostics support them.
`preview=TRUE` labels a provisional view; it never confirms metadata or overrides
failed QC. Figures need verified identities, adequate imaging and a suitable
caption before publication. Export settings do not establish scientific validity.

## 8. Interpret outputs and resolve warnings
=======
## 8. Interpret measurements and act on warnings
>>>>>>> origin/Rhizosphere-nitrogen-fate

| Output | What it measures |
|---|---|
| `MI_mean`, `MI_median` | Target-colony image darkness |
| `area_mm2`, `circularity`, `solidity` | Detected mask geometry, conditional on scale and segmentation |
| `delta_MI_facing` | Facing-minus-away darkness difference within a target |
| `radial_asymmetry_pct` | Toward/away radial asymmetry; alias of legacy `growth_inhibition_pct` |
| `gap_partner_mm` | Geometric gap to the detected central partner |
| `profiles` | Distance-from-edge ring summaries, not independent plates |
| `halo_status` | Resolved colour-zone candidate or unresolved boundary |

Control-referenced growth inhibition is `(C - T)/C * 100`, with a specified,
consistent growth outcome (e.g. radius or area). It is distinct from MI ratios
and from radial asymmetry. FunMel's matched assessment currently targets MI;
other outcomes and inhibition models must be specified separately.

| Warning/status | Meaning and action |
|---|---|
| Fitted illumination range | Pre-correction green-channel surface range, not residual error |
| `flat_field_clipped_fraction` | Fraction of dish pixels where gains exceed correction limits; inspect calibration |
| `residual_agar_range_pct` | Remaining spatial-bin median variation on fitted agar pixels; not validated colony-level error |
| `segmentation_trim_fraction` | Narrow target/central connection removed; inspect the refined outline |
| Undetected colony | No adequate region found; do not invent MI |
| `not_resolved` halo | Uncertain boundary; do not call it biological zero |
| Pending coefficient | Metadata/QC/missing-value issue; read its explicit reason |
| Inferential status other than `ok` | Review model/replication; descriptive ratios may still be available |

Flat-field fitting is not a substitute for comparable photography and exposure.
Use diffuse, consistent lighting and an appropriate reference where possible.
An agar reference is justified only for comparable, untinted medium; a reference
card needs known colour and suitable placement. Unrecoverable clipping or organism
colour gradients cannot be solved reliably by an image-only illumination model.
